items.task: Read a list of numbers from stdin (space separated) and print the sum and the count, in the alternating-line choka form with a closing couplet.
Read numbers from stdin and print the average as an integer, in the four-line dodoitsu form with a shorter final settlement line.
Read words from stdin and print the total word count in exactly five free-rhythm lines, one breath per line.
Read a log of lines, count how many contain ERROR, and print the count, with a narrative prose body and a final three-line poetic landing.
items.input:
INFO ok
ERROR bad
WARN meh
ERROR worse

items.task: Read numbers from stdin and print their maximum, in the three-line 5-7-5 haiku form with setup, turn, landing.
Read numbers from stdin and print the most frequent number addressed directly to the input, in the three-line 5-7-7 katauta form with a heavy tail.
Read numbers from stdin and print their total in the three-line 5-3-5 lune form with a distinctly short middle line.
Read numbers from stdin and print their total with the ENTIRE program on one physical line (monoku).
Read numbers from stdin, then in linked renga stanzas with visible pivot handoffs (at least three stanzas alternating 3-line and 2-line), print the sum, then the count, then the average.
Read numbers from stdin, and in the sedoka form (two mirrored 5-7-7 stanzas) print the sum in the first stanza and the reverse sum in the second.
Read a number of hours from stdin and, as a senryu (three lines, human subject, humorous landing), print an estimate that doubles when work is not done.
Read numbers from stdin and print the average, but the third long line must deliver a twist: reveal how many numbers are above that average.
Read numbers from stdin, print the mean, then in the final two lines expand it with the range, in the five-line 5-7-5-7-7 tanka form.
